The Competition Commission of India (CCI) is a statutory and quasi-judicial body established to promote fair competition in Indian markets, prevent anti-competitive practices, protect consumer interests, and ensure freedom of trade.

items: CCI is a statutory and quasi-judicial body, NOT a constitutional body.
Exam questions frequently test the key mandate of the CCI: promoting fair competition, preventing anti-competitive practices, protecting consumer interests, and ensuring freedom of trade.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Competition Commission of India (CCI) functions as a statutory and quasi-judicial body.
Its principal objective is to enforce fair competition across Indian markets.
It actively prevents anti-competitive practices and protects consumer interests.
It ensures the freedom of trade carried on by other participants in Indian markets.
